record.vts_authority: Havenmeester van Rotterdam (Port of Rotterdam Authority, Division Harbour Master), also Rijkshavenmeester regio Rotterdam-Rijnmond, VTS authority
record.vts_centre: Traffic Center Hook of Holland (Verkeerscentrale Hoek van Holland) and Traffic Center Botlek
record.vts_boundary_basis: PIG 2026 gives the Rotterdam VTS service area as 'Extending 38 nautical miles seawards of the port entrance' (P-S7). The official sector chart in the 2026 VHF procedure (Bijlage 2, P-S8; legally published P-S9) shows the Maas North traffic lanes north of the MN2-MN3 line within the area shaded as Sector Maas Approach (VHF 1). Distance test from the North Mole head (51 59'.67N 004 02'.84E) using Circ.67 positions (P-S1): whole scheme lies about 7.5 to 23 nm from the entrance (52 07'.1N to 52 22'.7N), inside 38 nm. Note: the statutory Rotterdam approach area (STZ Bijlage 1(f), P-S10) ends at the inner ends of the Maas TSSs (buoys MN3, MN2, MNW2, MNW3-MW4, MW5), so statutory powers (traffic instructions, navigational assistance) do not extend over the TSS; the association rests on the VTS service area (information/traffic organisation).
record.reporting_boundary_basis: Outside WETREP (scheme lies east of the WETREP limit line B/NL border to 52 12'N UK coast, P-S5) and all other Part I systems (P-S6). No Dutch national reporting system for the EEZ (P-S16, P-S17). The arrival report to Sector Maas Approach VHF 1 'from sea' is a VTS reporting duty (P-S8), recorded under the VTS, not as an MRS.
record.evidence_summary: Maas North lies in the approach covered by Rotterdam VTS Sector Maas Approach: within the stated 38 nm service area and inside the sector chart. Its southern end abuts the Pilot Maas sector / Maas Centre precautionary area. No mandatory reporting scheme applies; the VHF 1 arrival report is part of the VTS.
record.source_date: Port Information Guide Jan 2026; VHF procedure v2.0 Feb 2026 (Stcrt. 2026, 8272, in force 20 Feb 2026); COLREG.2/Circ.67 (in force 1 Jun 2017)
record.unresolved_issue: VTS area outer limit is stated only as '38 nautical miles seawards of the port entrance' plus a schematic chart; no coordinate boundary found. Statutory approach area stops at the TSS southern end. Coordinator may treat coverage as moderate-confidence.

record.coastal_state_s: Netherlands (IMO B-II/10); south-western part may lie in Belgian or UK EEZ waters, not verified
record.vts_boundary_basis: No VTS found. Scheme (51 27'-51 50'N, 002 02'-002 38'E, P-S1) is 50+ nm from the Rotterdam entrance, beyond the 38 nm Rotterdam VTS area (P-S7); it lies north of the Scheldt VTS seaward limit (about 51 23.6'-51 28.75'N between 002 19'E and 002 56'E, P-S20, 2014 folder). UK and Belgian VTS not checked beyond this.
record.reporting_authority: WETREP participating coastal States (per MSC.190(79) coverage points: United Kingdom, Ireland, France, Spain, Portugal, Belgium), reports to the nearest participating coastal station
record.reporting_boundary_basis: WETREP applies to every kind of oil tanker of more than 600 tonnes deadweight carrying heavy crude oil, heavy fuel oil or bitumen and tar (MSC.190(79) annex para 1.1): tanker-specific. Its north-eastern limit is the straight line from point 19 (51 22'25"N 003 21'52".5E) to point 20 (52 12'N UK east coast, about 001 37'E), confirmed on the chartlet (P-S5). Testing the Circ.67 positions (P-S1) against that line: all south-western and central positions (79, 80, 83, 84, 86) are 25-56' of longitude inside; the north-eastern corner positions (81, 82, 85, 87) lie within about 1-2' of the line (on it within plotting precision). Effectively the whole scheme is inside WETREP, with the NE extremity on the boundary. Outside CALDOVREP (P-S19).
record.evidence_summary: Inside the WETREP (VRS-0005) reporting area on the Part I boundary coordinates (near-full; NE end on the limit line). Applies to heavy-grade oil tankers only. No VTS coverage established; outside Rotterdam and (per 2014 chart) Scheldt VTS areas.
record.source_date: MSC.190(79) 6 Dec 2004; COLREG.2/Circ.67 20 May 2016; VTS-Scheldegebied folder v4.0 Aug 2014
record.unresolved_issue: WETREP boundary test is by computation from the resolution vertices (UK coast point longitude taken as about 001 37'E); the NE extremity sits on the line. Belgian/UK VTS absence not verified from a current official list; Scheldt VTS limit source is a 2014 folder.
record.vts_leads: Scheldt VTS (Wandelaar Approach, VHF 60) adjoins to the south; not coverage

record.vts_authority: Directeur Centraal Nautisch Beheer Noordzeekanaalgebied (Harbour Master and VTS authority; Port of Amsterdam / Rijkswaterstaat joint nautical management)
record.vts_centre: Not named in the regulation (traffic centre IJmuiden is a lead)
record.vts_sector: Sector IJmuiden, VHF 61 (12 nm zone); IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 is a supporting information-only channel outside the VTS sector
record.vts_boundary_basis: The VTS area at sea is the territorial sea within a 12 nm radius of the IJmuiden breakwater heads, including the extended IJ-geul (P-S12); the statutory IJmuiden approach area uses a 12 nm arc from reference point 52 27'.9N 004 32'.1E (P-S10). IJmuiden West Inner spans 004 07'-004 20'.35E (Circ.64, P-S2). Its eastern end (e.g. (16) 52 30'.52N 004 20'.35E, about 7.6 nm) lies inside 12 nm; the 12 nm arc crosses the scheme near 004 12'.6E, so roughly the eastern 4-5 nm (less if the territorial-sea limit is tighter) is inside and the western part is outside. Partial.
record.reporting_boundary_basis: No Part I system (P-S6); outside WETREP (P-S5). No Dutch reporting system under STZ art. 5a or the EEZ regulation was found (P-S10, P-S17). Arrival report at 12 nm to Sector IJmuiden VHF 61 and the report to IJmuiden Approaches VHF 7 'as soon as VHF contact is possible' are VTS / port-approach duties of the same authority (P-S12), not a separate MRS.
record.evidence_summary: Eastern portion of IJmuiden West Inner lies inside the 12 nm VTS area of the North Sea Canal Area (Sector IJmuiden, VHF 61); western portion outside, in the information-only IJmuiden Approaches (VHF 7) area. No mandatory reporting scheme.
record.source_date: VTS communication regulation v2.0 10 Sep 2025 (in force 30 Sep 2025); STZ version 1 Jan 2025; COLREG.2/Circ.64 4 Dec 2012 (in force 1 Aug 2013)
record.unresolved_issue: Exact split point depends on whether the 12 nm is measured from the breakwater heads or the STZ reference point and on the territorial-sea limit; partial coverage itself is not in doubt. Name of the traffic centre not stated in the regulation.
record.vts_leads: IJmuiden Approaches (VHF 7), information service only, covers the rest of the scheme per the Appendix I chart; not treated as VTS coverage
record.prior_lead_outcome: corrected: 'VTS only' (partial) confirmed from current sources (P-S2 coordinates now retrieved, P-S12 v2.0 of Sep 2025); VTS name and authority restated per the regulation and STZ designation
